inputs: A sanitized YouTube API artifact JSON file written outside Company OS, carrying no token, no header and no query string
An operator-supplied deliverable id, deliverable kind and format for each video whose readings cross into the analytics ledger
invariants: This package performs no network access and holds no credential: the authenticated fetch runs outside Company OS and leaves a file, which is the only input.
Every reading it commits carries measurement=interval, so a windowed API value can never collide with a cumulative Studio or Data API reading of the same metric.
An unavailable metric stays unavailable with a stated reason and is never normalized to zero.
An observation id is derived from what was measured - api, channel, video, deliverable, metric, window, measurement - never from fetch time, file path or the value.
A replayed pull is a no-op; a revised value for an existing identity is refused as a conflict and nothing is written, not even the source record.
Incomplete retrieval becomes DataScope(complete=False, excludes=...) naming the video ids that did not come back, never a silently shorter list.
Provider payload and normalized evidence stay distinct fields of one append-only envelope, digested over a single canonical basis.
outputs: YouTubeArtifact: validated channel, video, interval-analytics and retrieval-completeness evidence parsed from one artifact file
ApiArtifactSource and interval MetricObservation records for the analytics ledger, both identified by content rather than by fetch
An append-only evidence envelope with one digest, and secret-free API call telemetry carried through from the fetch
purpose: Turns a sanitized YouTube API artifact, produced by an authenticated fetcher outside Company OS, into validated channel, video and interval analytics evidence, and bridges per-video readings into the analytics ledger by reading a file, never a network.
risks: The artifact is only as good as the fetch that wrote it; a malformed or hand-edited file is rejected on validation, but a truthful-looking wrong one is not.
YouTube analytics can be delayed or revised, so a second pull of the same window surfaces as a conflict for a person to resolve, never a silent update.
Subscriber counts can be hidden or rounded by YouTube; that arrives as an unavailable reading with a reason rather than as a number.
The video-id to deliverable mapping is operator-supplied, so a wrong mapping attaches real readings to the wrong deliverable without any signal.
title: Network-free YouTube artifact ingestion
